title: A save overtaken in the queue never opens the database
body:
## Summary
saveStep's early out for a superseded save was checked at call time, one line after the slot was claimed, so it could never fire.

## Description
lib/steps/saveStep.ts:27-33 (before) claimed the slot then tested `slot.stillNewest()` immediately; every overtaken save still opened an IndexedDB connection inside its chain link and abandoned in the transaction. The check now runs at the head of the inIssueOrder link (lib/steps/saveStep.ts:30-37).

## Flow
- three saveStep calls to one key in one tick
- before: each link calls withStore -> openDb
- after: links 1 and 2 see a newer ticket and return superseded without opening

## Expected impact
Fewer connections per burst of saves; outcomes unchanged. Could break: nothing observed, in-transaction guard unchanged.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - superseded saves skip openDb
Before: 3 indexedDB.open calls for 3 same-tick saves
After: 1
Method: gate - new dal-real-engine case, seeded red on the old saveStep
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: tests/golden-path/dal-real-engine.probe.spec.ts 'a save superseded while it waits its turn never opens the database': Received 3 (before), 1 (after)

title: Retire the v1 step store's read/write path: no production code calls it
body:
## Summary
readStep, loadStep, saveStep, patchStep, readRecord, withStore and saveOrder (~447 LOC across 7 files) have zero production callers; only probes drive them.

## Description
git grep for calls of saveStep|loadStep|readStep|patchStep|readRecord outside lib/steps finds none in app/, lib/, components/, workers/, pipeline/ or packages/ (the readStep hits in lib/foundry/scout/budget.ts and lib/producers are a different function). The live dependents are narrow: reportStorageTrouble (lib/identityEviction.ts:302,390, reached only via components/ui/HarnessBridge.tsx), defineRecord/malformed/isPlainObject/RecordRefusal (lib/score/ads/record.ts, lib/frames/picture/migrate.ts), and the shape types packages/domain/src/steps cites. The v1 IDB rows are read for import by lib/studioArchive*.ts through lib/studioDb.ts directly, not through lib/steps. docs/next/migration-plan.md section 6: each phase deletes the v1 code it replaces. Also unobserved: the trouble channel has 0 production subscribers (onStorageTrouble only in dal-real-engine), so identityEviction's reportStorageTrouble publishes into nothing.

## Flow
- walk the import graph from app/, workers/, pipeline/ entries; list lib/steps exports actually called
- move reportStorageTrouble's caller to its own report (or @gt/ui/storage) and keep recordRegistry's pure decode half
- delete readStep/saveStep/patchStep/withStore/saveOrder/troubleChannel/okChannel and the probes that only pin them (score-takes step half, identity-and-writes claimSaveSlot cases, storage-remedy, dal-real-engine's step cases); update tests/mutants/registry.ts:207

## Expected impact
Roughly 447 LOC and ~5 probe files of v1 behaviour leave; nothing a user reaches changes. Could break: HarnessBridge's eviction report, if the reporter move is wrong.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - v1 code with no caller removed
Before: 7 write/read-path exports, 0 production call sites
After: 0 exports (predicted)
Method: simulation - grep-measured callers; the deletion spans tests and the mutant registry outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: git grep -nE '\b(saveStep|loadStep|readStep|patchStep|readRecord)\(' -- . ':!lib/steps' ':!.claude' ':!docs' -> only tests/, lib/foundry/scout/budget.ts:144 and lib/producers/scoutSceneActs.ts:141 (an unrelated readStep(k) helper)
instrument: an import-graph walk from app/, workers/, pipeline/ entry points that counts call sites of each lib/steps export (Before 0 for the 7); the full npm test + test:unit green after the deletion
drain_note: needs a human-sized plan: ~5 probes, registry, a reporter move

title: A throwing trouble listener breaks saveStep's never-reject promise
body:
## Summary
troubleChannel's report() and resolveTroubleWhere() call listeners unguarded inside withStore, so one throwing subscriber makes saveStep reject or turns a landed write into a reported failure.

## Description
lib/steps/withStore.ts:73 calls trouble() -> report() (lib/steps/troubleChannel.ts:36-40) inside the catch; a listener throw escapes withStore and saveStep rejects, against lib/steps/saveStep.ts:14-16. On the success path noteStorageOk -> resolveTroubleWhere notifies inside the try, so a throw is classified as a failed write after the put committed. Today the only subscriber is a test, so it is latent; moot if the retirement card lands.

## Flow
- subscribe a throwing listener via onStorageTrouble
- saveStep against a store that fails -> rejected promise
- fix: notify each listener in its own try and rethrow asynchronously (queueMicrotask) so the error stays visible

## Expected impact
No user-visible change today (no production subscriber).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - listener isolation
Before: 2 of 2 notify sites can break the promise (walked)
After: 0 (predicted)
Method: simulation - code walk; a fake-indexeddb case would decide it
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: lib/steps/troubleChannel.ts:38 listeners.forEach((l) => l()); called from lib/steps/withStore.ts:63 (catch) and okChannel noteStorageOk (try)
instrument: dal-real-engine case: onStorageTrouble(() => { throw }) then saveStep on a store with the steps store deleted; assert it resolves ok:false

title: patchStep and the issue-order chain have no driving test
body:
## Summary
No test calls patchStep or inIssueOrder; the save-then-patch ordering and decide-throw abort are pinned only in prose.

## Description
lib/steps/patchStep.ts:23-41 promises a failed read or a throwing decide writes nothing, and lib/steps/saveOrder.ts:70-86 promises a save issued before a patch lands first. grep -rn 'patchStep(\|inIssueOrder' tests packages/*/test -> only a source mention in step-record-literal-keys. Moot if the retirement card lands.

## Flow
- saveStep then patchStep in one tick -> patch merges onto saved record
- decide throws -> nothing written, trouble kind failed
- two patches in one tick -> both fields land

## Expected impact
Pins the module's two ordering guarantees if it stays.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - coverage of declared behaviour
Before: 0 of 3 cases pinned
After: 3 of 3 (predicted)
Method: simulation - cases named, not written: building tests on a path with no production caller waits on the retirement decision
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: git grep -n 'patchStep(\|inIssueOrder(' -- tests packages -> 0 call sites
instrument: three dal-real-engine cases (fake-indexeddb) seeded red by reverting inIssueOrder to a pass-through

title: readStep sits outside the issue-order chain, so a same-tick read can miss a save
body:
## Summary
readStep opens its own transaction without joining inIssueOrder, so a read issued after a save in the same tick can return what the save is about to replace.

## Description
lib/steps/readStep.ts:14-28 calls withStore directly; saveStep/patchStep queue through lib/steps/saveOrder.ts:89. The deleted saveWatchers.ts documented exactly this race (the Research Clear) and patched it for one reader; with that reader retired there is no consumer, so it is latent.

## Flow
- saveStep(k, A) then readStep(k) in one tick
- the read's transaction can open first and return the old value
- fix: route readStep through inIssueOrder(k) (reads then wait for queued writes)

## Expected impact
Read-your-write within a tick. No production reader today.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - read-your-write
Before: not guaranteed (walked)
After: guaranteed (predicted)
Method: simulation - a fake-indexeddb case can decide whether the engine orders it anyway
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: lib/steps/readStep.ts:18 withStore('read', ...) with no inIssueOrder; git show 1d93bfc9^:lib/steps/saveWatchers.ts:5-20 describes the race
instrument: dal-real-engine case: void saveStep(k,A); readStep(k) same tick; assert data A; run 20 times

title: v1 classify calls a SecurityError 'failed' where @gt/ui's says 'unavailable'
body:
## Summary
Two classifiers of one rule disagree: packages/ui/src/storage/trouble.ts:38 maps SecurityError to unavailable, lib/steps/reportTrouble.ts:18-25 falls through to failed.

## Description
A blocked-storage browser throws SecurityError on indexedDB.open; v1 would voice it as 'the browser refused the operation' instead of 'cannot store anything'. The only live producer is identityEviction's reportStorageTrouble, and no production surface subscribes, so it is unobserved; moot if the retirement card lands.

## Flow

- v1: failed; v2: unavailable
- fix: one line in reportTrouble.ts + a storage-remedy case

## Expected impact
Consistent vocabulary if v1 stays.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one rule, one answer
Before: 1 of 4 recognised names classified differently
After: 0 (predicted)
Method: simulation - read both classifiers
Result: better
Gate: none
